title: CI's suite sharded by file, macOS first; the cut the only whole-suite run; tagged tree scans at every landing
body:
## What this is

Release review action 3 (O7 with O8 and O9), ruled into the next devbin release (vc decision 177, 2026-11-14). It has three parts: shard CI's suite by file, macOS first; make the cut the only whole-suite run; and run the tagged tree-scan arms at every landing. This issue scopes the work. Nothing is built yet.

## The record it starts from

The figures are measured unless marked INFERRED. The sources are the review (sections 3b, 3c and 5) and 0.1.24's candidate run, 43426783134, read 2026-11-14.

- **The green cut** has taken 63 to 69 minutes in every release since 0.1.19. One job bounds it: GitHub's 3-CPU macOS runner.
- **The candidate leg** has taken 3533 to 4314 s. In 0.1.24 it ran 12:37:43Z to 13:49:11Z, 4288 s.
  - 0.1.24's macOS job ran its lanes for 70.7 minutes, of a 71.3-minute job. Setup is 21 s, so the suite is the job.
  - Ubuntu's lane ran 23.3 minutes on 4 CPUs.
- **The macOS runner is CPU-bound.** 3 jobs and 24 jobs give the same wall. No job count fixes it. Only more runners do, or a bigger one (O12, the fallback).
- **Attempts per release** were 2 to 5, from 0.1.19 to 0.1.23.
- **Whole-suite executions** to ship 0.1.23 were about 21, across rhadamanth, kovacs and CI.
- **Where the reds came from:**
  - tree-scan arms not run before landing (0.1.20, seven arms; 0.1.21, one arm);
  - proof runs outside the gates' environment (three of 0.1.23's four reds);
  - infrastructure.

  The whole-suite kit runs before the cut prevented none of them.

## Action 1 is in, and need not land first

The shards need cutting from measured times, and those times are there. Per-file wall times, the serial lane's time, and the load at both ends shipped in 0.1.24 (0345-1, 03942c76). Unheld progress shipped with them (0346-1).

0.1.24's candidate run printed all of it on every platform:
- **macOS:** 70 files, 12463 file-seconds at 3 jobs. contract.bats was slowest at 1384.7 s, then releasecut.bats at 909.5 s and dispatch.bats at 854.1 s.
- **Ubuntu:** 70 files, 5360 file-seconds at 4 jobs. releasecut.bats was slowest at 412.7 s.

What action 1 lacks for this work is a kept record. The times are lines in a CI log, which GitHub expires. A shard split needs them committed, so they can be read and refreshed.

## The split, from those times (INFERRED)

The method is greedy, longest first. Each shard's wall is the larger of its file-seconds over the runner's jobs, or its longest file:

| macOS shards | Longest shard | Bound by           |
| ------------ | ------------- | ------------------ |
| 1 (today)    | 70.7 min      | the whole suite    |
| 2            | 34.6 min      | total work         |
| 3            | 23.1 min      | contract.bats      |
| 4            | 23.1 min      | contract.bats      |
| 4, contract.bats under 17 min | 17.3 min | total work |
| 6, contract.bats under 11 min | 11.5 min | total work |

Ubuntu in 2 shards comes to about 11 minutes each.

**contract.bats is the floor from three shards up.** Two things lift it:
- O9's second half: drop the clean-tree half of the 0155 arm, whose lint run `check all` has already made.
- A split of the file.

The per-file times are measured under three-way contention. A shard runs at that same contention, so they carry over. How far a file's own within-file parallelism shortens it alone is not established.

## What changes, and in which files

### O7: shard CI by file

- `.github/workflows/tests.yml`:
  - test-macos becomes a matrix over shard indices. It starts at 4 shards and stays macOS-only, so the matrix key is the number.
  - test-linux becomes 2 shards.
  - Test Summary's `needs:` and its checks read each matrix job's result.
  - A shard that GitHub never assigned a runner to stays "not run", not red. The existing `abandoned` path in Test Summary already says this for one job.
  - WSL is unchanged. It blocks nothing (O11).
- `lib/bats-lanes`:
  - A shard setting, eg `DEVBIN_TEST_SHARD=<i>/<n>`, picks one shard's files. The selection is a pure function of the file list, the committed weights and `<n>`.
  - A file with no weight goes in, with a default weight, so no file is left out.
  - The "every test exactly once" check holds per shard: the files named, counted by bats.
  - The run prints its shard's file list and the shard's own count.
- **The sum across shards:** Test Summary (or a step each shard writes to) proves the shards together ran every file once. The shards' counts must add up to one untagged `bats --count`. This is O7's one new proof: no shard lost a file, and none ran a file twice.
- **The weights file:** a new committed record, eg `tests/unit/.lanes-weights.tsv`, of file and seconds per platform. It is cut from a candidate run's lanes lines and refreshed by a verb, never by hand, from a CI log or a local seal. Where it lives, and whether doctor or a contract arm checks that it names every test file, is to settle in the unit.
- **Tests:**
  - tests/unit/ci-workflow.bats holds the trigger, the jobs' conditions and the summary's needs to the workflow. It changes with the matrix.
  - tests/unit/ci-state.bats holds `release.ci.summary` to the job's name. The name is unchanged, so this should only need a reread.
  - New bats-lanes arms for shard selection, the default weight and the per-shard count go beside the lanes arms (testhandler.bats and builtins.bats, which hold them today).
- `bin/.devbin/config.yaml`: `release.ci.wait` drops from 90m once the shards are measured. The 90m allowed for macOS's whole suite plus a queue.
- `lib/cmd/ci-state` and `lib/cmd/release` (the candidate leg, release_ci_verdict in lib/release.steps): these read the run's summary job. The reading so far finds nothing in them that names a test job, so sharding should leave them alone. The unit confirms that by grep.
- docs/releasing.md (the candidate leg) and docs/configuration.md (`release.ci.wait`): the shard count and why.

### O8: the cut is the only whole suite

This is mostly a ruling for vc and hv, not code. A fix runs its own arms plus the tagged tree scans, under `release gates`' environment. No seat books a whole-suite kit on rhadamanth or kovacs before a cut. The cut runs everything once per leg. A red cut before the tag still costs a reset, as now.

The code side:
- `.github/workflows/tests.yml`: the release commit's push to main runs Ubuntu again, 25 to 31 minutes, on a commit its candidate already proved, and the cut never waits for it. Skipping it is an option. Keeping it is also defensible, as main's own badge. That is a call for hv.
- docs/releasing.md: say the rule where seats read it.

### O9: tagged tree scans at every landing

- **A tag, eg `treescan`, on each arm that walks lib/ and bin/** (shfmt's tree, `git ls-files`, or a grep over every shipped file). The review counts about 20 arms. The reading so far finds tree-walking arms in tests/unit/contract.bats, workroom.bats, runlog.bats, releasesnapshot.bats, lineendings.bats and fleet.bats. The 0079 arm in updatenotice.bats and the critic arm in shell-gate-critic.bats are also candidates. The unit lists them by title first.
- **A fast verb:**
  - `bin/devbin test scans` runs `bats --filter-tags treescan` over tests/unit, in the lanes runner.
  - It is declared in `bin/.devbin/config.yaml` under `commands.test.options`.
  - It is run by bin/.devbin/cmd/test, which owns the test command today.
- **A guard, so an arm that walks the tree cannot land untagged.** It would be a contract arm or a check that finds untagged arms using the scan helpers. Whether one can be written without being a regex over test bodies is not yet known.
- **contract.bats's 0155 arm:** keep the planted-breach half and drop the clean-tree half, which `check all` has already run in the same gates. That also lifts O7's floor.
- **"At every landing":** the landing scripts are seat tooling outside this tree, and vc points them at `test scans`. Nothing in devbin itself lands a unit.

## Criteria, each measured against the record

| Measure | The record | Target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The candidate leg, on the RELEASE seal | 3533 to 4314 s (0.1.24: 4288 s) | 1500 s or less at 4 macOS shards with contract.bats as it is; about 1100 s once contract.bats is under 17 min (INFERRED from the split above) |
| A green cut's wall | about 63 min (63 to 69 since 0.1.19) | local plus kovacs, about 32 min (MEASURED serialised in 0.1.23's cut). The candidate leg is no longer the bound |
| Attempts per release | 2 to 5 | 1 |
| Whole-suite executions per release | about 21 | one per leg per attempt: local, kovacs, and CI's Ubuntu, macOS (its shards summing to one) and WSL, so 5 at one attempt |
| Coverage | every test on every platform at the release commit | the same, proven by the shards' summed count |

## Not yet known

- **Runner assignment for more macOS jobs.** The record has one 80-minute wait (0.1.22) and one job never assigned (41994585531). A public repository's limit on concurrent macOS jobs is lower than Linux's. Four shards may queue behind each other, and how often is not established.
- Whether a file's within-file parallelism makes it shorter alone than its contended time.
- Whether any tree scan in a consumer's suite should take the same tag. This issue is devbin's own suite.
- Whether skipping the post-release Ubuntu run on main is wanted (O8, above).

## Options, none chosen

- Shard by committed weights (above), or by a fixed hand list of files per shard. A hand list goes stale as files grow, and the weights file is what keeps it right.
- Start macOS at 3 shards, the floor contract.bats sets today, and go to 4 when contract.bats is split. Or start at 4.
- Split contract.bats in this issue, or leave it to O4 (split the long files), which needs these times too.


## Record

- 0357-2 landed at 608a0ef4 (2026-11-14): the lanes runner's shard (`DEVBIN_TEST_SHARD=i/n`), the committed weights file `tests/unit/.lanes-weights` cut from run 43426783134, `bin/devbin test --weights`, and `bats-lanes --plan`.
- 0357-3's plan, approved (vc, 2026-11-14): 4 macOS shards and 2 Ubuntu, n read from `strategy.job-total`; lint into both gate lists, on shard 1 alone, with the 0155 arm's clean-tree half dropped and its corpus control kept on a fixture; `--weights` merging several logs per system; the shards' sum proven statically (no new actions). The macOS count is hv's open question: 4 is built, and 3 is a one-line change.
- Follow-on, not in this issue's units: lower `release.ci.wait` from 90m once a sharded candidate's seconds are on a RELEASE seal.
- Known, no work now: a matrix leg GitHub never assigns a runner may read as FAILED in Test Summary rather than NOT RUN (0238 wrote that case for a single job). It fails safe: the cut still refuses.
